Class ToonCodec

java.lang.Object
org.roux.toon.ToonCodec
public final class ToonCodec extends Object
The ToonCodec writes and reads the text payload of one message. One encoded payload starts with the line m[1]{r,ts,tok,x}:. The next line is the role word, the time, the token count, and the text, separated by commas. decode(byte[], long, byte, long, int) keeps the role, the time, and the token count from the frame header. The text comes from the payload. The type refuses construction. // @aa-sdd L40 aa-sdd-source-prose.md#ToonCodec roux-v1.md

    • encode

      public static byte[] encode(byte role, long timestampEpochMs, int tokenCount, String text)
      The method encodes one message as UTF-8 bytes. A null text is written as an empty body. The role byte is written as its role word. // @aa-sdd G-13 aetheris-stages-1-3.finalize.md
      Parameters:
      role - The role is the role byte.
      timestampEpochMs - The time is the epoch milliseconds stored with the message.
      tokenCount - The token count is the number stored with the message.
      text - The text is the message body, or null.
      Returns:
      The bytes are the encoded payload.

    • decode

      public static DecodedFrame decode(byte[] payload, long messageId, byte headerRole, long headerTs, int headerTokens)
      The method builds a DecodedFrame from a payload. A null payload is read as an empty string. The role, the time, and the token count come from the arguments. The text is the field after the third comma.
      Parameters:
      payload - The payload is the encoded bytes, or null.
      messageId - The message id is the number that locates the frame.
      headerRole - The role is the role byte from the frame header.
      headerTs - The time is the epoch milliseconds from the frame header.
      headerTokens - The token count is the number from the frame header.
      Returns:
      The frame is the decoded message.

    • appendTableRow

      public static void appendTableRow(StringBuilder out, String role, long ts, int tok, String text)
      The method appends one table row. An empty builder first receives the line messages[0]{r,ts,tok,x}:. A null text is written as an empty body. The row ends with a newline.
      Parameters:
      out - The builder receives the row.
      role - The role is the role word.
      ts - The time is the epoch milliseconds.
      tok - The token count is the number stored with the message.
      text - The text is the message body, or null.

    • appendQuoted

      private static void appendQuoted(StringBuilder sb, String text)
      The method appends text, quoting it when a comma or a special character is present. An empty string is quoted. A quote, a backslash, a newline, a carriage return, and a tab are escaped inside quotes.
      Parameters:

      text - The text is the raw body.

      private static boolean needsQuote(String text)
      The method reports whether a body must be quoted. An empty string must be quoted. A comma, a quote, a newline, a carriage return, a colon, or a bracket must be quoted.
      Parameters:
      text - The text is the body to inspect.
      Returns:
      The flag is true when quotes are required.

    • extractText

      private static String extractText(String raw)
      The method returns the text field of one payload. The field is the text after the third comma on the line after the first newline. A payload with no newline uses the whole string. Fewer than three commas returns an empty string. A trailing newline or carriage return is removed.
      Parameters:
      raw - The raw value is the payload string.
      Returns:
      The text is the message body, or an empty string.

    • unquote

      private static String unquote(String field)
      The method removes quotes and escape sequences from one field. A field that does not start with a quote is returned unchanged. \\n becomes a newline. \\r becomes a carriage return. \\t becomes a tab. A quoted backslash or quote keeps the following character.
      Parameters:
      field - The field is the text that may be quoted.
      Returns:
      The text is the unescaped body.

    • parseMessageTable

      public static String[] parseMessageTable(String table)
      The method reads a message table into role and text pairs. A null table returns null. Lines are split on a newline, and a trailing carriage return is removed. A blank line after the header is skipped. The header must start with messages[ and end with ]{r,ts,tok,x}:. The number between the brackets is the row count. A header that is not that shape, a count that is not a number, or a negative count returns null. A row that splitMessageRow(String) cannot split returns null. A row count that does not match the data rows returns null. A count of zero and no data rows returns a zero-length array. Each pair is the role, then the text.
      Parameters:
      table - The table is the messages[N]{r,ts,tok,x}: text, or null.
      Returns:
      The array is role, text, role, text, or null when the table is refused.

    • pairConversation

      public static String[] pairConversation(String[] flat)
      The method pairs user text with the assistant text that follows it. A null array returns null. An odd length returns null because the values are not role and text pairs. A null text is read as an empty string. A user row and the assistant row after it are one cell. A user row with no assistant yet is a cell with an empty reply. An assistant row with no user ahead of it is a cell with an empty prompt. A system row, a tool row, and any other role are left out. A list with no user or assistant row returns a zero-length array.
      Parameters:
      flat - The flat array is role, text pairs from parseMessageTable(String), or null.
      Returns:
      The array is prompt, reply, prompt, reply, or null when the input is not pairs.

    • conversationTable

      public static String conversationTable(List<String> roles, List<String> texts)
      The method writes the table that parseMessageTable(String) reads. A null role list or a null text list returns null. Lists of different lengths return null. Two empty lists return messages[0]{r,ts,tok,x}: and a newline. Each row uses a timestamp of zero and a token count of zero. A null text is written as an empty body.
      Parameters:
      roles - The roles are the role words, one per row.
      texts - The texts are the row bodies, one per role.
      Returns:
      The table is the encoded text, or null when the lists disagree.

    • splitMessageRow

      private static String[] splitMessageRow(String line)
      The method splits one table row into a role and a text. The role is the text before the first comma. The text is the field after the third comma. A comma inside quotes stays in the text. A backslash inside quotes skips the next character. An empty role, a missing first comma, or a missing third comma returns null. A role character that is not a lowercase letter or an underscore returns null. The text is passed through unquote(String).
      Parameters:
      line - The line is one table row.
      Returns:
      The pair is the role and the text, or null when the row is refused.
